rows: Severe thunderstorms moved into Lee County in the late afternoon. They began producing severe winds as they approached US77, knocking down trees and power lines from near Lincoln eastward to near Dime Box. The storm also destroyed outbuildings and damaged several mobile homes alo…

High winds blew an 18-wheel trailer off a bridge and into a creek along US77 2 miles north of Lexington. Other severe thunderstorm winds knocked down trees and power lines in the city of Lexington. Some residents were left without power for few hours.
Quarter size hail was reported along Highway 141.
Newspaper in Lexington reported trees down in the city of Lexington.
The Lee County Sheriff reported hail up to quarter size near the town of Northrup.
A resident reported nickel size hail which damaged a pickup truck.
A farmer in Ledbetter reported damage to his barn along with trees blown down.
A barn roof was partially destroyed by strong thunderstorm winds. Survey could not find a definitive tornado track so damage is being recorded as strong thunderstorm winds.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 50 knots which knocked down a large tree across Hwy 121 in Dime Box.

A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph. A dead tree was knocked down and the winds lifted a trampoline onto the roof of a house. The trampoline had been staked to the ground with two feet of rebar.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 58 mph which broke several tree limbs and knocked down some dead trees along FM 2440 west of Giddings. This storm also produced penny size hail.

Thunderstorms produced wind gusts estimated at 50 mph which blew down several trees and destroyed some buildings. A church gym was heavily damaged. Several trees were blown down along Highway 21 and throughout the county.
A mobile home was rolled over and destroyed.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 50 mph that broke tree limbs up to six inches in diameter.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 58 mph that blew down several large Oak trees blocking FM 448 at FM 2239.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 58 mph that damaged the underpinning of a mobile home, a porch, a barn, a well house, a fence, and multiple trees.

A small EF0 tornado touched down just southeast of Lexington. A combination of eye witnesses, storm chasers, and a NWS survey concluded that it produced little damage in mainly rural areas southeast of Lexington. A few trees were damaged near the area but little in the way of a p…
Hail size estimated at one inch.
Numerous reports of trees down and hail in the town of Lexington. Hail size was not determined in the report.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 58 mph that damaged trees off Private Rd. 1271 near Giddings.

A high end EF-0 tornado touched down damaging a Ramada Hotel on Highway 290 east of the city of Giddings. Most of the damage consisted of uprooted trees rooted in wet soils while other damage included a destroyed outbuilding, whose debris were lofted into the Ramada Hotel causing…
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts measured at 78 mph at knocked down a tree across Hwy 77 north of Lexington.
A thunderstorm produced half dollar size hail in Giddings.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts measured at 75 mph in Giddings. The gusty winds were accompanied with quarter size hail.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Giddings. The hail was accompanied by winds gusts estimated at 75 mph.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that snapped large Oak trees on the south side of Giddings.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail at the Tanglewood Christian Camp.
A thunderstorm produced tennis ball size hail in Northrup.
A thunderstorm produced golf ball size hail in Giddings.
A thunderstorm produced tennis ball size hail off FM 141 southeast of Dime Box.
A thunderstorm produced one inch hail near Manheim.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that blew down a tree on US 77 north of Giddings.
A thunderstorm produced a measured wind gust of 52 kts. at the Giddings-Lee County Airport.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that knocked down some large tree limbs between Manheim and Giddings.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail just west of Giddings.
A thunderstorm produced nickel size hail in Lexington.
A thunderstorm produced penny size hail in Dime Box.
A thunderstorm produced quarter to half dollar size hail between Fedor and Lexington.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Lexington.
A thunderstorm produced nickel to golf ball size hail east of Lexington. Hail fell for 15 minutes.
A thunderstorm produced ping pong ball to golf ball size hail that coverd the ground in Lexington.
A thunderstorm produced two inch hail in Lexington.

A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Giddings.
